003import static io.jstach.rainbowgum.spi.RainbowGumServiceProvider.findProviders;
004
005import java.lang.System.Logger.Level;
006import java.util.ArrayList;
007import java.util.Collection;
008import java.util.EnumSet;
009import java.util.List;
010import java.util.Locale;
011import java.util.Objects;
012import java.util.ServiceLoader;
013import java.util.Set;
014import java.util.concurrent.ConcurrentHashMap;
015import java.util.concurrent.CopyOnWriteArrayList;
016import java.util.concurrent.atomic.AtomicReference;
017import java.util.function.Consumer;
018
019import org.jspecify.annotations.Nullable;
020
021import io.jstach.rainbowgum.LevelResolver.LevelConfig;
022import io.jstach.rainbowgum.LogConfig.ChangePublisher;
023import io.jstach.rainbowgum.LogEvent.Caller.CallerType;
024import io.jstach.rainbowgum.spi.RainbowGumServiceProvider;
025import io.jstach.rainbowgum.spi.RainbowGumServiceProvider.Configurator;
026import io.jstach.rainbowgum.spi.RainbowGumServiceProvider.PropertiesProvider;

028/**
029 * The configuration of a RainbowGum. In some other logging implementations this is called
030 * "context".
031 * <p>
032 * A config can be used by only one {@link RainbowGum}, even after that RainbowGum is
033 * closed. Using it for another {@link RainbowGum.Builder} throws
034 * {@link IllegalStateException}; build a new config instead.
035 */
036public sealed interface LogConfig extends LogProperty.PropertySupport {
037
038        /**
039         * When to dump bootstrap alerts to the fail-safe output.
040         */
041        public enum DebugModeType {
042
043                /**
044                 * Do not dump alerts beyond the normal alert startup policy.
045                 */
046                OFF,
047                /**
048                 * Dump the failure and collected alerts if building the config fails.
049                 */
050                ERROR,
051                /**
052                 * Dump collected alerts after every successful config build and on build failure.
053                 */
054                INFO,
055                /**
056                 * Dump collected alerts as in {@link #INFO}, and print a {@link LogReporter}
057                 * report after Rainbow Gum starts.
058                 */
059                ALL;
060
061                static DebugModeType parse(String value) {
062                        String v = value.toUpperCase(Locale.ROOT);
063                        return switch (v) {
064                                case "FALSE" -> OFF;
065                                case "TRUE" -> ALL;
066                                default -> LogProperty.enumValue(DebugModeType.class, value, "true", "false");
067                        };
068                }
069
070        }
071
072        /**
073         * String key value properties.
074         * @return properties.
075         */
076        @Override
077        public LogProperties properties();
078
079        /**
080         * Effective debug mode collected while this configuration was built. A system
081         * property value, when present, takes precedence over the builder setting.
082         * @return debug mode.
083         */
084        public DebugModeType debugMode();
085
086        /**
087         * Level resolver for resolving levels from logger names.
088         * @return level resolver.
089         */
090        public LevelConfig levelResolver();
091
092        /**
093         * Output provider that uses URI to find output.
094         * @return output provider.
095         */
096        public LogOutputRegistry outputRegistry();
097
098        /**
099         * Provides encoders by URI scheme.
100         * @return encoder registry.
101         */
102        public LogEncoderRegistry encoderRegistry();
103
104        /**
105         * Provides publishers by URI scheme.
106         * @return changePublisher registry.
107         */
108        public LogPublisherRegistry publisherRegistry();
109
110        /**
111         * Creates a builder for making LogConfig.
112         * @return builder.
113         */
114        public static Builder builder() {
115                return new Builder();
116        }
117
118        /**
119         * An event changePublisher to publish configuration changes.
120         * @return changePublisher.
121         */
122        public ChangePublisher changePublisher();
123
124        /**
125         * Service registry are custom services needed by plugins particularly during the
126         * initialization process.
127         * @return registry.
128         */
129        public ServiceRegistry serviceRegistry();
130
131        /**
132         * Alerts about problems with the logging system itself (as opposed to application
133         * logging routed through the {@link LogRouter}).
134         * @return alerts.
135         */
136        public LogAlerts alerts();
137
138        /**
139         * Metrics about the logging system itself (as opposed to application logging routed
140         * through the {@link LogRouter}).
141         * @return metrics.
142         */
143        public LogMetrics metrics();
144
145        /**
146         * Accounts for every logger name a facade implementation has vended.
147         * @return logger registry.
148         */
149        public LoggerRegistry loggerRegistry();
150
151        /**
152         * Accounts for logger names, and which {@link LoggerAPI} vended them, registered via
153         * {@link #registerLoggerName(LoggerAPI, String)}, deliberately without exposing the
154         * accumulated names/APIs themselves: the one supported way to see them is
155         * {@link LogReporter.Section#LOGGERS}/{@link LogReporter.Section#FACADES}.
156         */
157        interface LoggerRegistry {
158
159                /**
160                 * Registers that a logger with this name exists. Idempotent: registering the same
161                 * name more than once has no additional effect. The first time a given name is
162                 * registered this also increments {@link LogMetrics#LOGGER_NAMES_METRIC} on
163                 * {@link LogConfig#metrics()}, so the running total is cheap to observe (e.g. to
164                 * catch unbounded logger name usage) without ever having to size the accumulated
165                 * names themselves.
166                 * @param api which facade this name came through.
167                 * @param loggerName logger name.
168                 */
169                void registerLoggerName(LoggerAPI api, String loggerName);
170
171        }
172
173        /**
174         * Mixin for config support.
175         */
176        interface ConfigSupport extends LogProperty.PropertySupport {
177
178                /**
179                 * Provides config.
180                 * @return config.
181                 */
182                public LogConfig config();
183
184                @Override
185                default LogProperties properties() {
186                        return config().properties();
187                }
188
189        }
190
191        /**
192         * Config Change Publisher. By default this is enabled with
193         * {@value LogProperties#GLOBAL_CHANGE_PROPERTY} set to <code>true</code>, which then
194         * gates two independent, per-logger-name properties:
195         * {@value LogProperties#CHANGE_PREFIX} + {@value LogProperties#SEP} + logger name,
196         * set to a list of {@link ChangeType} or <code>true</code>/<code>false</code> to
197         * enable or disable all changes, and {@value LogProperties#CALLER_PREFIX} +
198         * {@value LogProperties#SEP} + logger name, set to a {@link CallerType} (or
199         * <code>true</code>/<code>false</code>) to control caller info. The two are resolved
200         * independently - one does not imply or override the other, even for overlapping
201         * logger name prefixes.
202         */
203        interface ChangePublisher {
204
205                /**
206                 * Subscribe to changes.
207                 * @param consumer consumer.
208                 */
209                public void subscribe(Consumer<? super LogConfig> consumer);
210
211                /**
212                 * Publish that there has been changes.
213                 */
214                public void publish();
215
216                /**
217                 * Test to see if <strong>any</strong> changes are enabled for a logger - either
218                 * {@link #allowedChanges(String)} is non-empty or {@link #callerType(String)} is
219                 * not {@link CallerType#NONE}.
220                 * @param loggerName logger name.
221                 * @return true if enabled.
222                 */
223                public boolean isEnabled(String loggerName);
224
225                /**
226                 * Returns what the logger is allowed to change.
227                 * @param loggerName logger name.
228                 * @return which things are allowed to change in the logger
229                 */
230                public Set<ChangeType> allowedChanges(String loggerName);
231
232                /**
233                 * The caller info strategy for a logger, resolved from
234                 * {@value LogProperties#CALLER_PREFIX}, independently of
235                 * {@link #allowedChanges(String)} /{@value LogProperties#CHANGE_PREFIX}. Unlike
236                 * {@link ChangeType#LEVEL}, which is genuinely re-evaluated on every
237                 * {@link #publish()}, this is resolved once when a logger is first created and
238                 * never revisited afterward - it reflects a static per-logger capability, not
239                 * something that changes at runtime.
240                 * @param loggerName logger name.
241                 * @return caller type, {@link CallerType#NONE} if not configured.
242                 */
243                public CallerType callerType(String loggerName);
244
245                /**
246                 * Whether caller info should be computed for a logger at all, regardless of which
247                 * non-{@link CallerType#NONE} strategy.
248                 * @param loggerName logger name.
249                 * @return true if caller info is enabled for this logger.
250                 */
251                default boolean callerInfoEnabled(String loggerName) {
252                        return callerType(loggerName) != CallerType.NONE;
253                }
254
255                /**
256                 * Changing type options.
257                 */
258                public enum ChangeType {
259
260                        /**
261                         * No changes are allowed. Synonymous with <code>false</code> - never actually
262                         * present in a {@link #allowedChanges(String)} result (that case is just the
263                         * empty set); this exists so a single malformed-vs-explicitly-off token can
264                         * be told apart while parsing, and so <code>false</code> is a real,
265                         * documented enum member rather than only a magic string.
266                         */
267                        NONE,
268                        /**
269                         * The logger is allowed to change levels.
270                         */
271                        LEVEL;
272
273                        static Set<ChangeType> parse(List<String> value) {
274                                if (value.isEmpty()) {
275                                        return Set.of();
276                                }
277                                var s = EnumSet.noneOf(ChangeType.class);
278                                for (var v : value) {
279                                        if (v.equalsIgnoreCase("true")) {
280                                                return EnumSet.complementOf(EnumSet.of(ChangeType.NONE));
281                                        }
282                                        var ct = ChangeType.parse(v);
283                                        if (ct == NONE) {
284                                                return EnumSet.noneOf(ChangeType.class);
285                                        }
286                                        s.add(ct);
287                                }
288                                return s;
289                        }
290
291                        static ChangeType parse(String value) {
292                                String v = value.toUpperCase(Locale.ROOT);
293                                return switch (v) {
294                                        case "FALSE" -> NONE;
295                                        default -> LogProperty.enumValue(ChangeType.class, value, "true", "false");
296                                };
297                        }
298
299                }
300
301        }
302
303        /**
304         * Builder for LogConfig.
305         * <p>
306         * <strong>NOTE:</strong> The service loader is not used by default with this builder.
307         * If the automatic discovery of components is desired call
308         * {@link #serviceLoader(ServiceLoader)}.
309         */
310        public static final class Builder extends LevelResolver.AbstractBuilder<Builder> {
311
312                private @Nullable ServiceRegistry serviceRegistry;
313
314                private @Nullable LogProperties logProperties;
315
316                private @Nullable ServiceLoader<RainbowGumServiceProvider> serviceLoader;
317
318                private final List<RainbowGumServiceProvider.Configurator> configurators = new ArrayList<>();
319
320                private final List<RainbowGumServiceProvider.PropertiesProvider> propertiesProviders = new ArrayList<>();
321
322                private DebugModeType debugMode = DebugModeType.OFF;
323
324                /**
325                 * Default constructor
326                 */
327                private Builder() {
328                }
329
330                /**
331                 * Sets log properties
332                 * @param logProperties log properties.
333                 * @return this.
334                 */
335                public Builder properties(LogProperties logProperties) {
336                        this.logProperties = logProperties;
337                        return this;
338                }
339
340                /**
341                 * Sets the debug mode used when the system property
342                 * {@value LogProperties#DEBUG_PROPERTY} is absent.
343                 * @param debugMode debug mode.
344                 * @return this.
345                 */
346                public Builder debug(DebugModeType debugMode) {
347                        this.debugMode = Objects.requireNonNull(debugMode);
348                        return this;
349                }
350
351                /**
352                 * Sets service registry
353                 * @param serviceRegistry service registry.
354                 * @return this.
355                 */
356                public Builder serviceRegistry(ServiceRegistry serviceRegistry) {
357                        this.serviceRegistry = serviceRegistry;
358                        return this;
359                }
360
361                /**
362                 * Add to configure LogConfig and ServiceRegistry.
363                 * @param configurator will run on build.
364                 * @return this.
365                 */
366                public Builder configurator(RainbowGumServiceProvider.Configurator configurator) {
367                        configurators.add(configurator);
368                        return this;
369                }
370
371                /**
372                 * Add properties.
373                 * @param propertiesProvider will run on build.
374                 * @return this.
375                 */
376                public Builder propertiesProvider(RainbowGumServiceProvider.PropertiesProvider propertiesProvider) {
377                        propertiesProviders.add(propertiesProvider);
378                        return this;
379                }
380
381                /**
382                 * Sets the service loader to use for loading components that were not set.
383                 * @param serviceLoader loader to use for missing components.
384                 * @return this.
385                 */
386                public Builder serviceLoader(ServiceLoader<RainbowGumServiceProvider> serviceLoader) {
387                        this.serviceLoader = serviceLoader;
388                        return this;
389                }
390
391                /**
392                 * Sets a default service loader to use for loading components that were not set.
393                 * This call will just call the {@link ServiceLoader} without providing a class
394                 * loader.
395                 * @return this.
396                 */
397                public Builder serviceLoader() {
398                        return this.serviceLoader(ServiceLoader.load(RainbowGumServiceProvider.class));
399                }
400
401                /**
402                 * Configures the builder with a function for ergonomics.
403                 * @param consumer passed the builder.
404                 * @return this.
405                 */
406                public Builder with(Consumer<? super Builder> consumer) {
407                        consumer.accept(this);
408                        return this;
409                }
410
411                /**
412                 * Builds LogConfig which will use the {@link ServiceLoader} if set to load
413                 * missing components and if not set will use static defaults.
414                 * @return log config
415                 */
416                public LogConfig build() {
417                        var prePropertiesAlerts = new SwappableLogAlerts();
418                        LogAlerts dumpAlerts = prePropertiesAlerts;
419                        boolean startingAlerts = false;
420                        DebugModeType debug = LogProperties.StandardProperties.SYSTEM_PROPERTIES
421                                .forKey(LogProperties.DEBUG_PROPERTY)
422                                .ofString()
423                                .map(DebugModeType::parse)
424                                .or(this.debugMode)
425                                .validateNow(Builder.class);
426                        try {
427                                ServiceRegistry serviceRegistry = this.serviceRegistry;
428                                LogProperties logProperties = this.logProperties;
429
430                                var serviceLoader = this.serviceLoader;
431                                var configurators = this.configurators;
432                                if (serviceRegistry == null) {
433                                        serviceRegistry = ServiceRegistry.of();
434                                }
435                                if (logProperties == null) {
436                                        List<LogProperties> props = new ArrayList<>();
437                                        for (var pp : propertiesProviders) {
438                                                prePropertiesAlerts.info(LogConfig.class, "Loading properties from "
439                                                                + LogReporter.Reportable.toString(pp, "unknown PropertiesProvider"));
440                                                props.addAll(pp.provideProperties(serviceRegistry, prePropertiesAlerts));
441                                        }
442                                        if (props.isEmpty() && serviceLoader != null) {
443                                                props.addAll(provideProperties(serviceRegistry, serviceLoader, prePropertiesAlerts));
444                                        }
445                                        /*
446                                         * LogProperties.of(List, LogProperties)'s fallback argument is only
447                                         * used when the list is empty, so SYSTEM_PROPERTIES has to be a real
448                                         * member of the list itself to always be included, not passed as that
449                                         * fallback: otherwise it silently disappears the moment any
450                                         * PropertiesProvider contributes anything at all (e.g.
451                                         * rainbowgum-micronaut5's own GLOBAL_CHANGE_PROPERTY layer), breaking
452                                         * every -D system property override for such an application with no
453                                         * warning.
454                                         */
455                                        props.add(LogProperties.StandardProperties.SYSTEM_PROPERTIES);
456                                        logProperties = LogProperties.of(props);
457
458                                }
459                                /*
460                                 * Built before DefaultLogConfig itself (rather than left for
461                                 * DefaultLogConfig's constructor to create, as before) specifically so
462                                 * buildGlobalResolver below can hand LogAlerts to the global level
463                                 * resolver's alerting wrapper - the global resolver is built before a
464                                 * full LogConfig exists to pull config.alerts() from, so alerts (and
465                                 * metrics, via alerts' own listener wiring) are constructed directly here
466                                 * instead. Capacity and logging.alerts.unobservedErrorsAction both come
467                                 * from logProperties as already resolved above - before any configurator
468                                 * runs, the same as everything else built directly in this method - see
469                                 * DefaultLogAlerts.of(...) for how the two are validated together.
470                                 */
471                                LogAlerts alerts = DefaultLogAlerts.of(logProperties);
472                                LogMetrics metrics = new DefaultLogMetrics();
473                                var levelResolver = this.buildGlobalResolver(logProperties, alerts);
474                                var config = new DefaultLogConfig(serviceRegistry, logProperties, levelResolver, alerts, metrics,
475                                                debug);
476                                // The config constructor installs the metrics listener before replay.
477                                prePropertiesAlerts.drainTo(alerts);
478                                dumpAlerts = alerts;
479                                if (serviceLoader != null) {
480                                        configurators = new ArrayList<>(configurators);
481                                        findProviders(serviceLoader, Configurator.class).forEach(configurators::add);
482                                }
483                                if (!configurators.isEmpty()) {
484                                        for (var configurator : configurators) {
485                                                alerts.info(LogConfig.class, "Adding configurator: "
486                                                                + LogReporter.Reportable.toString(configurator, "unknown Configurator"));
487                                        }
488                                        /*
489                                         * TODO two-pass config: configurators run after config (and therefore
490                                         * the global level resolver above) already exists, so a configurator
491                                         * that contributes additional property sources or otherwise changes
492                                         * what the level resolver should have seen is invisible to it - the
493                                         * resolver was already built from logProperties as it stood before
494                                         * any configurator ran. A more correct design would run configurators
495                                         * first, then rebuild whatever is purely derived from properties
496                                         * (starting with the level resolver) a second time against the
497                                         * now-fully-configured LogConfig. Not done here - see todo.md.
498                                         */
499                                        RainbowGumServiceProvider.Configurator.runConfigurators(configurators.stream(), config);
500                                }
501                                /*
502                                 * Deliberately last: alerts already resolved
503                                 * LogAlerts.UnobservedErrorsAction at construction above, but only now,
504                                 * once configurators have had their chance to record alerts and/or
505                                 * register a real Listener, does "should I report/refuse to start"
506                                 * actually mean anything - by construction nothing has had a chance to
507                                 * register one before this point.
508                                 */
509                                // start() itself reports the backlog before throwing for FAIL.
510                                startingAlerts = true;
511                                alerts.start(config);
512                                if (debug == DebugModeType.INFO || debug == DebugModeType.ALL) {
513                                        dumpSuccessfulBuild(alerts);
514                                }
515                                return config;
516                        }
517                        catch (RuntimeException | Error e) {
518                                if (debug != DebugModeType.OFF && !startingAlerts) {
519                                        dumpBuildFailure(dumpAlerts, e);
520                                }
521                                throw e;
522                        }
523                }
524
525                private static void dumpSuccessfulBuild(LogAlerts alerts) {
526                        var events = alerts.dump();
527                        MetaLog.error(LogEventFactory.of(LogConfig.class.getName())
528                                .eventNoArg(Level.INFO, "LogConfig built; dumping " + events.size() + " alert(s)", null));
529                        for (var event : events) {
530                                MetaLog.error(event);
531                        }
532                }
533
534                /* Throwable.addSuppressed rejects self-suppression. */
535                @SuppressWarnings("ReferenceEquality")
536                private static void dumpBuildFailure(LogAlerts alerts, Throwable failure) {
537                        try {
538                                var events = alerts.dump();
539                                MetaLog.error(LogConfig.class, "LogConfig build failed; dumping " + events.size() + " alert(s)",
540                                                failure);
541                                for (var event : events) {
542                                        MetaLog.error(event);
543                                }
544                        }
545                        catch (Throwable dumpFailure) {
546                                if (dumpFailure != failure) {
547                                        failure.addSuppressed(dumpFailure);
548                                }
549                        }
550                }
551
552                LevelConfig buildGlobalResolver(LogProperties logProperties, LogAlerts alerts) {
553                        LevelConfig levelResolver = LevelConfig
554                                .of(List.of(ConfigLevelResolver.of(logProperties), GroupLevelResolver.of(logProperties)));
555                        var config = buildLevelConfigOrNull();
556                        if (config != null) {
557                                levelResolver = LevelConfig.of(List.<LevelConfig>of(config, levelResolver));
558                        }
559                        return new AlertingLevelConfig(levelResolver, alerts);
560                }
561
562                private static List<LogProperties> provideProperties(ServiceRegistry registry,
563                                ServiceLoader<RainbowGumServiceProvider> loader, LogAlerts alerts) {
564                        List<LogProperties> props = new ArrayList<>();
565                        for (var provider : findProviders(loader, PropertiesProvider.class).toList()) {
566                                alerts.info(LogConfig.class, "Loading properties from "
567                                                + LogReporter.Reportable.toString(provider, "unknown PropertiesProvider"));
568                                props.addAll(provider.provideProperties(registry, alerts));
569                        }
570                        return props;
571                }
572
573                @Override
574                protected Builder self() {
575                        return this;
576                }
577
578        }
579
580}
581
582abstract class AbstractChangePublisher implements ChangePublisher {
583
584        /*
585         * TODO Ideally this would be a concurrent weak hashmap. The reasoning is we may want
586         * a configuration where SLF4J loggers are not stored in concurrent hash map but some
587         * sort of GC friendly cache or not cached at all. If they subscribe to changes the
588         * loggers will never be GCed.
589         *
590         * Consequently the functional Consumer interface might not be the best choice.
591         */
592        private final Collection<Consumer<? super LogConfig>> consumers = new CopyOnWriteArrayList<Consumer<? super LogConfig>>();
593
594        /*
595         * Same shape as LevelResolver.java's CachedLevelResolver: allowedChanges(name) is
596         * only ever called once per never-before-seen logger name (RainbowGumLoggerFactory
597         * caches the resulting Logger forever afterward), so a ConcurrentHashMap here matches
598         * the exact call pattern that made a ConcurrentHashMap the right tradeoff there too.
599         */
600        private final ConcurrentHashMap<String, Set<ChangeType>> changesCache = new ConcurrentHashMap<>();
601
602        /*
603         * Sibling to changesCache, not folded into it - CallerType is resolved from its own
604         * logging.caller.<name> property, independent of logging.change.<name>, so it gets
605         * its own map rather than a combined per-name struct (one map per concern).
606         */
607        private final ConcurrentHashMap<String, CallerType> callerTypeCache = new ConcurrentHashMap<>();
608
609        protected abstract LogConfig reload();
610
611        protected abstract LogConfig config();
612
613        @Override
614        public void publish() {
615                changesCache.clear();
616                callerTypeCache.clear();
617                LogConfig config = reload();
618                for (var c : consumers) {
619                        c.accept(config);
620                }
621        }
622
623        @Override
624        public void subscribe(Consumer<? super LogConfig> consumer) {
625                consumers.add(consumer);
626        }
627
628        @Override
629        public boolean isEnabled(String loggerName) {
630                return !allowedChanges(loggerName).isEmpty() || callerType(loggerName) != CallerType.NONE;
631        }
632
633        @Override
634        public Set<ChangeType> allowedChanges(String loggerName) {
635                return changesCache.computeIfAbsent(loggerName, n -> {
636                        /*
637                         * findOrNull walks the logger-name hierarchy (closest match wins, see its own
638                         * javadoc) trying each candidate key in turn - per candidate, resolve it as a
639                         * LogProperty and only return null (telling findOrNull to keep walking up)
640                         * when the key is genuinely Missing there. A present-but-malformed value is a
641                         * Result.Error, not a Missing - it must stop the walk right there rather than
642                         * silently falling through to a less specific ancestor's value.
643                         */
644                        LogProperty.Result<Set<ChangeType>> result = config().properties()
645                                .findOrNull(LogProperties.CHANGE_PREFIX, n, (props, fullKey) -> {
646                                        LogProperty.Result<Set<ChangeType>> r = props.forKey(fullKey).ofList().map(ChangeType::parse);
647                                        return r instanceof LogProperty.Result.Missing ? null : r;
648                                });
649                        if (result == null) {
650                                return Set.of();
651                        }
652                        try {
653                                return result.validateNow(ChangePublisher.class);
654                        }
655                        catch (LogProperty.ValidationException e) {
656                                /*
657                                 * A malformed logging.change.<name> value must not be able to break
658                                 * logging itself. ConcurrentHashMap#computeIfAbsent leaves nothing cached
659                                 * when the mapping function throws, so without catching this a bad
660                                 * property would re-parse and re-alert on every single allowedChanges(n)
661                                 * call for this logger name, not just once - same amplification risk
662                                 * CachedLevelResolver guards against for level properties. Fall back to
663                                 * "nothing allowed to change" and alert exactly once per logger name
664                                 * instead, since the fallback value is itself cached above just like a
665                                 * successful parse would be. validateNow's own Missing = failure
666                                 * semantics are moot here - the lambda above never returns a Missing
667                                 * result to it in the first place.
668                                 */
669                                config().alerts().error(ChangePublisher.class, e);
670                                return Set.of();
671                        }
672                });
673        }
674
675        @Override
676        public CallerType callerType(String loggerName) {
677                return callerTypeCache.computeIfAbsent(loggerName, n -> {
678                        LogProperty.Result<CallerType> result = config().properties()
679                                .findOrNull(LogProperties.CALLER_PREFIX, n, (props, fullKey) -> {
680                                        LogProperty.Result<CallerType> r = props.forKey(fullKey).ofString().map(CallerType::parse);
681                                        return r instanceof LogProperty.Result.Missing ? null : r;
682                                });
683                        if (result == null) {
684                                return CallerType.NONE;
685                        }
686                        try {
687                                return result.validateNow(ChangePublisher.class);
688                        }
689                        catch (LogProperty.ValidationException e) {
690                                /*
691                                 * Same reasoning as allowedChanges()'s catch above: a malformed (or
692                                 * pre-split, e.g. the old "caller" token that used to live in
693                                 * logging.change.<name>) logging.caller.<name> value alerts once and
694                                 * falls back to CallerType.NONE, cached, rather than re-parsing and
695                                 * re-alerting on every call.
696                                 */
697                                config().alerts().error(ChangePublisher.class, e);
698                                return CallerType.NONE;
699                        }
700                });
701        }
702
703}

735final class DefaultLogConfig implements LogConfig {
736
737        private final ServiceRegistry registry;
738
739        private final LogProperties properties;
740
741        private final DebugModeType debugMode;
742
743        private final LevelConfig levelResolver;
744
745        private final ChangePublisher changePublisher;
746
747        private final LogOutputRegistry outputRegistry;
748
749        private final LogEncoderRegistry encoderRegistry;
750
751        private final LogPublisherRegistry publisherRegistry;
752
753        private final LogAlerts alerts;
754
755        private final LogMetrics metrics;
756
757        private final LoggerRegistry loggerRegistry;
758
759        /*
760         * Registered outputs/appenders, alert listeners, and service registry closeables are
761         * never reset when a RainbowGum closes, so a second RainbowGum on this config would
762         * fail on duplicate output names, flush/reopen the first one's closed appenders, and
763         * lose alert listeners. Ownership and built state change together in one CAS so
764         * concurrent build() calls cannot both win.
765         */
766        private final AtomicReference<@Nullable Claim> claim = new AtomicReference<>();
767
768        private record Claim(Object owner, boolean built) {
769        }
770
771        DefaultLogConfig(ServiceRegistry registry, LogProperties properties, LevelConfig levelResolver, LogAlerts alerts,
772                        LogMetrics metrics, DebugModeType debugMode) {
773                super();
774                this.registry = registry;
775                this.properties = properties;
776                this.debugMode = debugMode;
777                this.levelResolver = levelResolver;
778                this.alerts = alerts;
779                this.metrics = metrics;
780                this.loggerRegistry = new DefaultLoggerRegistry(metrics);
781                boolean changeable = properties.forKey(LogProperties.GLOBAL_CHANGE_PROPERTY)
782                        .ofBoolean()
783                        .or(false)
784                        .validateNow(DefaultLogConfig.class);
785                this.changePublisher = changeable ? new DefaultChangePublisher() : IgnoreChangePublisher.INSTANT;
786                applyGlobalAppenderReentrantLockProperty(properties);
787                applyGlobalThreadLocalDisabledProperty(properties);
788                applyGlobalOptimizeProperty(properties);
789                this.outputRegistry = DefaultOutputRegistry.of(registry);
790                this.encoderRegistry = DefaultEncoderRegistry.of();
791                this.publisherRegistry = DefaultPublisherRegistry.of();
792                /*
793                 * addInternalListener, not addListener: a passive in-process counter nobody has
794                 * wired an exporter to does not count as "someone is watching" for
795                 * LogAlerts.UnobservedErrorsAction's purposes - see DefaultLogAlerts's own
796                 * comment on hasExternalListener. Config alerts is always a DefaultLogAlerts;
797                 * SwappableLogAlerts is only passed to PropertiesProviders before config exists.
798                 */
799                ((DefaultLogAlerts) this.alerts).addInternalListener(event -> {
800                        switch (event.level()) {
801                                case ERROR -> this.metrics.errorCounter(event.loggerName(), 1);
802                                case WARNING -> this.metrics.warnCounter(event.loggerName(), 1);
803                                default -> this.metrics.infoCounter(event.loggerName(), 1);
804                        }
805                });
806        }
807
808        void bind(Object owner) {
809                acquire(owner, false);
810        }
811
812        void markBuilt(Object owner) {
813                acquire(owner, true);
814        }
815
816        @SuppressWarnings("ReferenceEquality") // owner is a specific builder instance
817        private void acquire(Object owner, boolean build) {
818                while (true) {
819                        var current = claim.get();
820                        if (current != null && current.owner() != owner) {
821                                throw new IllegalStateException("LogConfig is already used by another RainbowGum. "
822                                                + "A LogConfig can only be used by one RainbowGum, even after that RainbowGum is closed. "
823                                                + "Build a new LogConfig instead.");
824                        }
825                        if (current != null && current.built() && build) {
826                                throw new IllegalStateException("This builder already built a RainbowGum. "
827                                                + "A LogConfig can only be used by one RainbowGum. Build a new LogConfig instead.");
828                        }
829                        if (current != null && (current.built() || !build)) {
830                                return;
831                        }
832                        if (claim.compareAndSet(current, new Claim(owner, build))) {
833                                return;
834                        }
835                }
836        }
837
838        /*
839         * Deliberately mutates process-wide static state (AbstractLogAppender's field) rather
840         * than per-instance state - LogProperties#GLOBAL_APPENDER_REENTRANT_LOCK_PROPERTY is
841         * a global guarantee by design (see its javadoc), not a per-LogConfig setting.
842         * Last-writer-wins if multiple RainbowGum instances with different values coexist in
843         * one JVM - an accepted tradeoff for a property whose whole point is a process-wide
844         * guarantee independent of any single instance's configuration.
845         */
846        private static void applyGlobalAppenderReentrantLockProperty(LogProperties properties) {
847                AbstractLogAppender.forceReentrantLockAppenders = properties
848                        .forKey(LogProperties.GLOBAL_APPENDER_REENTRANT_LOCK_PROPERTY)
849                        .ofBoolean()
850                        .or(false)
851                        .validateNow(DefaultLogConfig.class);
852        }
853
854        /*
855         * An enum (TRUE/FALSE) rather than .ofBoolean() deliberately, unlike its sibling just
856         * above - a typo'd value here (e.g. "yse") fails loudly through the existing
857         * Property/Result machinery instead of silently resolving to "not disabled", which is
858         * the wrong failure mode for a property whose whole point is a hard, otherwise
859         * easy-to-silently-miss guarantee.
860         */
861        private enum ThreadLocalDisabled {
862
863                TRUE, FALSE;
864
865                static ThreadLocalDisabled parse(String value) {
866                        return LogProperty.enumValue(ThreadLocalDisabled.class, value);
867                }
868
869        }
870
871        /*
872         * Same last-writer-wins/process-wide-guarantee tradeoff as
873         * applyGlobalAppenderReentrantLockProperty just above - see that method's comment.
874         * rainbowgum-slf4j independently reads this same property key at its own SLF4J
875         * provider initialize() touchpoint to decide whether to disable MDC too - see
876         * LogProperties#GLOBAL_THREADLOCAL_DISABLED_PROPERTY's javadoc for why that is two
877         * independent readers rather than one shared flag.
878         */
879        private static void applyGlobalThreadLocalDisabledProperty(LogProperties properties) {
880                AbstractLogAppender.forceNoThreadLocalAppenders = properties
881                        .forKey(LogProperties.GLOBAL_THREADLOCAL_DISABLED_PROPERTY)
882                        .ofString()
883                        .map(ThreadLocalDisabled::parse)
884                        .or(ThreadLocalDisabled.FALSE)
885                        .validateNow(DefaultLogConfig.class) == ThreadLocalDisabled.TRUE;
886        }
887
888        /*
889         * Same enum-not-boolean reasoning as ThreadLocalDisabled above. Unlike the other two
890         * global properties this one is not a "force/guarantee" downgrade applied after a
891         * type is already resolved - it changes what the *default* resolves to when nothing
892         * more specific (an explicit appenderType(...)/useGetBytes(...) call, or a more
893         * specific property) was set, so it is read into the same kind of process-wide static
894         * flag but consulted at a different point (LogAppender.Builder#build(),
895         * LogEncoder.Builder#build()) - see LogProperties#GLOBAL_OPTIMIZE_PROPERTY's javadoc.
896         */
897        private enum GlobalOptimize {
898
899                TRUE, FALSE;
900
901                static GlobalOptimize parse(String value) {
902                        return LogProperty.enumValue(GlobalOptimize.class, value);
903                }
904
905        }
906
907        private static void applyGlobalOptimizeProperty(LogProperties properties) {
908                AbstractLogAppender.globalOptimizeEnabled = properties.forKey(LogProperties.GLOBAL_OPTIMIZE_PROPERTY)
909                        .ofString()
910                        .map(GlobalOptimize::parse)
911                        .or(GlobalOptimize.FALSE)
912                        .validateNow(DefaultLogConfig.class) == GlobalOptimize.TRUE;
913        }
914
915        class DefaultChangePublisher extends AbstractChangePublisher {
916
917                @Override
918                protected LogConfig config() {
919                        return DefaultLogConfig.this;
920                }
921
922                @Override

925                        return DefaultLogConfig.this;
926                }

928        }
929
930        @Override
931        public LogProperties properties() {
932                return properties;
933        }
934
935        @Override
936        public DebugModeType debugMode() {
937                return debugMode;
938        }
939
940        @Override
941        public LevelConfig levelResolver() {
942                return this.levelResolver;
943        }
944
945        @Override
946        public ServiceRegistry serviceRegistry() {
947                return this.registry;
948        }
949
950        @Override
951        public ChangePublisher changePublisher() {
952                return this.changePublisher;
953        }
954
955        @Override
956        public LogOutputRegistry outputRegistry() {
957                return this.outputRegistry;
958        }

960        @Override
961        public LogEncoderRegistry encoderRegistry() {
962                return this.encoderRegistry;
963        }

965        @Override

969
970        @Override
971        public LogAlerts alerts() {
972                return this.alerts;

975        @Override

987final class DefaultLoggerRegistry implements LogConfig.LoggerRegistry {
988
989        private final Set<String> loggerNames = ConcurrentHashMap.newKeySet();
990
991        private final Set<LoggerAPI> loggerAPIs = ConcurrentHashMap.newKeySet();
992
993        private final LogMetrics metrics;
994
995        DefaultLoggerRegistry(LogMetrics metrics) {
996                this.metrics = metrics;
997        }
998
999        @Override
1000        public void registerLoggerName(LoggerAPI api, String loggerName) {
1001                Objects.requireNonNull(api);
1002                loggerAPIs.add(api);
1003                if (loggerNames.add(loggerName)) {
1004                        metrics.infoCounter(LogMetrics.LOGGER_NAMES_METRIC, 1);
1005                }
1006        }
1007
1008        /*
1009         * Deliberately not on the LogConfig.LoggerRegistry interface itself (see its
1010         * javadoc): DefaultLogReporter downcasts to this package-private type to reach it,
1011         * the same pattern DefaultLogConfig's own constructor already uses to reach
1012         * DefaultLogAlerts#addInternalListener.
1013         */
1014        Set<String> loggerNames() {
1015                return Set.copyOf(loggerNames);
1016        }
1017
1018        /**
1019         * Every {@link LoggerAPI} registered so far via {@link #registerLoggerName}, not just
1020         * {@link LoggerAPI.Standard}: an application-provided {@link LoggerAPI} works too.
1021         * Same downcast-only visibility as {@link #loggerNames()}.
1022         * @return immutable snapshot.
1023         */
1024        Set<LoggerAPI> loggerAPIs() {
1025                return Set.copyOf(loggerAPIs);
1026        }
1027
1028}
